items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he had a five piece band, with Zoot Sims and myself

ctx.x: Did you work with Buddy Rich?

Yeah, Buddy Rich, 1951, he got a band together, he had a five piece band, with Zoot Sims and myself, a piano player later ended up with Patti Page, his name was Rocky Carluccio, a bass player, Teddy Kotak, and I can’t think of the guitar player’s name. But we played all up in Boston at the High Hat, oh, we played all over with Buddy. In fact, the first time I heard Philly Joe Jones we were playing in Philadelphia at a club called the 721 Club up on Wyalusing and Philly Joe was playing right across the street. I…
And he wouldn’t put up with any discrimination

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I get a call to come to the Apollo to play with the Four Brothers

ctx.x: You were based in New York.
I wasn’t thinking about leaving New York. And I get a call to come to the Apollo to play with the Four Brothers, there was [Gerry] Mulligan, Zoot [Sims], Stan [Getz] and I forget

who else was the Four Brothers. But I worked at the Apollo quite a few times with different bands. I would play at the Park across from Manhattan there, Palisades, play there for a week. I just played all around New York.

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Zoot Sims and I were roommates. ... But Zoot and I, we played with Buddy for a long time.

ctx.x: Yes, that was a small band, wasn't it?

Small band. Went with Herbie Fields and then I played around Philadelphia and New York, Providence, Rhode Island, all around the East Coast. Then I went with Jazz at the Philharmonic. I did that for about two years. Because it only lasted about six weeks a year at that time, anyway, you know, steady. So then I joined Buddy Rich's small band. We played at the Pop City, Royal Roost, played at Philadelphia, the Strand in Boston, around the East Coast, every place, you know. Zoot Sims and I were roommates. He had two…
But Zoot and I, we played with Buddy for a long time. And then I free lanced around New York, played the Apollo with different bands like Stan Getz, when he had a band to go in there.
